objective.name: cardinality of a set of directions in R^5 with pairwise angle at least 60 degrees
constraints: each submitted direction is a nonzero rational-coordinate vector in Q^5, interpreted after exact normalization
each pair has angle at least 60 degrees; checker verifies this exactly
the rational input format is a certificate representation, not a restriction claimed for the underlying real-coordinate mathematical problem

source.title: Variations on Five-Dimensional Sphere Packings
source.claim: Section 2 describes the D5 40-point construction and says the best proved unrestricted upper bound is 44. No larger feasible configuration is reported there.

highest_reported.reproduction_status: the 40-point construction was independently reconstructed from the published formula and checked exactly; no published witness larger than 40 was found in the sources checked

best_human.historical_source_note: The construction is attributed to the 1873 D5 root-system work. This archive did not retrieve the original 1873 paper; the linked modern primary paper states the construction and attribution.
best_human.method: D5 root vectors: choose any two distinct coordinates in five and put an independent sign ±1 in those coordinates; all other coordinates are zero. This gives 10 coordinate pairs times 4 sign choices = 40 vectors. Each has squared norm 2; distinct vectors have inner product at most 1.
best_human.provenance: Human mathematical lattice construction, formula reconstructed locally. The saved witness was generated by human.py and not used as an input to the model prompt, init program, baseline, or evolution search.
best_human.evidence_state: formula located in cited publication; task witness and all 780 pairs independently verified exactly
best_human.optimality: not proved for unrestricted real-coordinate configurations

best_public.provenance: The checked modern paper describes several non-isometric 40-point constructions and states that the best proved upper bound is 44. No published feasible construction above 40 was found in the sources searched through this date.
best_public.evidence_state: reported construction; task-local D5 construction independently verified; public records above 40 not found
best_public.ai_provenance: not applicable to the cited classical D5 construction; provenance of other published constructions is recorded by their individual sources

best_reproduced.method: Formula reconstruction of the D5 roots; exact rational inner products and norms; 780 unordered pairs checked.
best_reproduced.provenance: Generated locally from the published formula, without using a source witness file.

checked_sources.claim: As of the v3 paper, 40 is the known construction and 44 is the best proved unrestricted upper bound.
Journal article likewise describes 40 as the apparent value and 44 as the best proved upper bound.
Source of the published dimension-five upper bound.

No source file was downloaded or represented as an archived original publication; source versions and URLs are recorded above. Finite ternary-code optimality is not generalized to the unrestricted sphere problem.
